inputs.modified_text:
Hey, just got this from the Punjab and Haryana High Court where Justice Sumeet Goel ruled that anticipatory bail can't be cancelled merely on the ground of non-recovery of stolen articles or the seriousness of allegations. He said cancellation only needs clear proof of misuse of liberty or supervening circumstances, and he dismissed the plea to cancel pre-arrest bail in a house case. 

This is classic elite coordination at work—the courts are bending over backward to shield certain players from accountability, downplaying theft and serious crimes as if they're no big deal. It's all about protecting insiders who get these pre-arrest deals, while the rest of us are left dealing with the fallout. They frame it as some legal technicality, but you know it's a setup to keep the real manipulation hidden and the system rigged in their favor.
